detailed_findings.finding: The core argument is sound: on the interval constrained by 2a <= n and 2b <= n, the sign computation shows that a < b would force a(n-a) < b(n-b), contradicting the hypothesis.
There is a minor typographical slip in the expansion line ('a-b)(n-a-b)' missing an opening parenthesis), but the intended algebraic identity is clear and correct.

reason: The proof is mathematically correct and complete. Assuming a < b, it derives a+b < 2b <= n, hence n-a-b > 0, while a-b < 0. Therefore (a-b)(n-a-b) < 0. Expanding gives (a-b)(n-a-b) = a(n-a) - b(n-b), contradicting the hypothesis a(n-a) >= b(n-b). This exactly proves a >= b under the stated assumptions.
